nodes.summary: If $r \ne 0$ lies in the span of vectors $\varphi_i$, then $\langle\varphi_i, r\rangle \ne 0$ for some $i$: otherwise $r$ would be orthogonal to the span, hence to itself. This makes the greedy selection ratio $\rho(r)$ well defined for a nonzero residual.

nodes.summary: For a subspace $L$ with orthogonal projection $P_L$ and any $s$, the residual $s - P_L s$ is orthogonal to every $w \in L$: $\langle w, s - P_L s\rangle = 0$. In particular an atom already selected has zero correlation with the residual and is not selected again.
